messages.subject: measurement starts at midnight error
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I am processing some GENEActiv datasets where Part 1 runs fine, but Part 2 gives the following error:

1measurement starts at midnight or there is no midnightmeasurement ends at midnight or there is no midnightError in IMP$averageday[1:abs(difference), (mi - 1)] :
  subscript out of bounds

The datasets were set to start recording at 23:59.

I have tried the code with strategy 1 and 2, but get the same error with both and I have run the exact same code on other files with no problem. The bin files themselves seem fine when viewed in GENEActivPC and when converted to csv epoch files.

Do you have any suggestions as to what might be causing the problem?

Thanks,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] measurement starts at midnight error
parts:
Hi Alex,
The error message either indicates that it is a short measurement with no midnights or (less intuitive) that timestamp 00:00:00 does not occur in the measurement because Windows and Linux systems treat such timestamp differently. If you can send me the milestone file (.RData) then I should be able to address it in the package.
thanks,
Vincent

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: measurement starts at midnight error
parts:
Alex,
It was a different problem which only applies to measurements that are started between clock time 23:45 and 00:00 excluding 00:00 itself. Your measurement starts at 23:59. Underlying function g.getmeta always rounds the starting time of a measurement up to the first integer number of large time window blocks in an hour (default is 900 seconds = 15 minutes). This means that it tries to find the next 0, 15, 30, 45 minutes past the hour. I do this to ensure that extracted features between measurements and between days within a measurement can be aligned in a standardized way. My original implementation was a bit ugly for starting times in the last 15 minutes of a day.

I have now fixed this and I just uploaded a new version of the package (version 1.2-2) to the CRAN repository. If it is approved then it should be online in the upcoming days.
This means that you will have to reprocess that problematic accelerometer file with part 1.
Cheers,
Vincent
